title: Dow Wobbles as Boeing Plummets; Broadcom Surges After Anthropic Report – Live Market Update
body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped into modest territory on Tuesday, caught in a tug‑of‑war between a cautious Federal Reserve meeting and a sharp sell‑off in Boeing shares, while a surge in consumer confidence offered a counterbalance. Meanwhile, technology‑sector heavyweight Broadcom rallied after a report linked its AI‑chip subsidiary Anthropic to a promising new partnership, underscoring the market’s appetite for artificial‑intelligence plays even as aerospace earnings remain under pressure.

The Dow opened the session hovering near 33,800 points, but soon lost ground as investors digested the Federal Reserve’s opening remarks. The central bank signaled that policy tightening will likely continue, with officials emphasizing that inflation remains above target despite recent moderation. That dovetail of “higher‑for‑longer” rates and lingering price pressures nudged risk‑averse traders toward safer assets, pulling the Dow down about 0.3% by mid‑morning. The broader S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite mirrored the trend, each slipping roughly 0.4% as rate‑sensitive sectors like consumer discretionary and technology felt the pinch.

Boeing (BA) was the day's standout laggard, tumbling more than 5% after the aerospace giant disclosed weaker-than‑expected order intake for the quarter and warned of production bottlenecks at its 737 line. The company’s earnings preview highlighted a slowdown in commercial airline demand, especially from carriers still grappling with supply‑chain constraints and the lingering effects of the pandemic‑induced fleet retirements. Analysts pointed to the firm’s ongoing challenges in ramping up the 737 MAX and the financial strain of its defense contracts, which together have eroded investor confidence. The stock’s slide contributed significantly to the Dow’s underperformance, given Boeing’s heavy weighting in the index.

In contrast, Broadcom (AVGO) delivered a bright spot, climbing close to 4% after a Bloomberg report linked its AI chip subsidiary Anthropic to a new multi‑year collaboration with a major cloud provider. The partnership is expected to accelerate Anthropic’s model training capabilities, positioning Broadcom at the forefront of the next wave of generative‑AI hardware. Market participants praised the move as a validation of Broadcom’s strategic pivot toward high‑margin AI infrastructure, a sector that has been outpacing traditional semiconductor growth. The rally lifted the technology‑heavy Nasdaq, offsetting some of the broader market weakness.

Consumer sentiment data released earlier in the day added another layer of nuance. The University of Michigan’s preliminary index rose to 71.4, up from 70.2 the previous month, marking the strongest reading in nearly a year. The uptick reflects growing optimism about personal finances, employment prospects, and future spending. Retail stocks such as Target and Home Depot responded positively, each posting modest gains. However, the sentiment boost was not enough to fully counterbalance the macro‑economic headwinds stemming from the Fed’s stance and the aerospace sector’s woes.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching several key catalysts. The Federal Reserve’s next policy decision, slated for later this month, could either reinforce the current rate‑hike trajectory or signal a pause, a move that would likely reshape equity valuations across the board. Boeing’s upcoming quarterly earnings report will be a litmus test for whether the company can stabilize its production line and revive order flow, while Broadcom’s progress with Anthropic may set a benchmark for AI‑related earnings growth. In the meantime, the interplay between consumer confidence and monetary policy will continue to dictate the market’s rhythm, with investors poised to adjust positions as new data emerges.
